shared_elements: monolithic carved stone monument, taller than wide
anthropomorphic figure occupying the full height of the field
head with elaborate headdress/cap at the top
shallow incised or low-relief linear carving
horizontal band or belt-like element across the body
museum display setting with plinth and label
justification: Both are upright stone monuments dominated by a single anthropomorphic figure whose headdressed head occupies the top and whose torso, marked by band- and disc-like motifs, fills the lower field, which gives a loosely comparable vertical scheme. The decisive difference is the medium and manner: A is a flat, framed slab bearing a crisp profile figure in even low relief, while B is a bulky three-dimensional boulder with a frontal, volumetric head and faint, worn incisions spread over an irregular surface.
